_why: Rules and their expected verdicts as DATA, not as assertions buried in test
code. Shape borrowed from OpenFirma's `policy test fixture.toml` — the idea,
not the code; that project is GPL-3.0 and this one is MIT.
Rows are TEMPLATES, not finished strings, and that is not cosmetic: the first
version stored complete key-shaped strings and GitHub Push Protection refused
the push, naming two of them. It was right to. A fixture that looks exactly
like a credential is a credential as far as every scanner is concerned, and a
repository that trains people to click 'allow this secret' has taught them the
wrong reflex. The runner assembles prefix + fill at test time, so nothing in
the tree matches a scanner and the scanner under test still sees the real shape.
`allow` rows are load-bearing: a scanner that flags a placeholder in a README
teaches people to bypass it, and a bypassed guard is an off guard.

deny.why: the spelling the rule used to miss — an underscore before `secret` killed the \b
env-file spelling, also missed before the fix

deny.literal:
-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIEow==
-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----

allow.why: a placeholder in prose is not a secret
an env var reference — the thing we ask people to do

allow.content: # how to set your secret access key in the console

allow.why: a short token matching no rule
a truncated example, as docs write them
